newsitem.title: CHINA: RESEARCH ALERT - HUTCHISON TO OUTPERFORM.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - HUTCHISON TO OUTPERFORM.

text.p: Merrill Lynch said it had reiterated its accumulate recommendation on Hutchison Whampoa Ltd, with the stock expected to outperform due to strong fundamentals and further corporate restructuring.
"Hutchison has recently begun to outperform after an 18 months period of underperformance," Merrill Lynch said in a research report. "We expect further outperformance."

Merrill Lynch said it expected the stock to be re-rated due to strong fundamentals. Core profit, excluding exceptionals, was forecast to rise at a compound annual growth rate of 33 percent over 1996-99 with overall earnings growing at 16 percent.
Merrill Lynch said the main driving forces behind growth would be a progressive return in profits from property development and a turnaround in the telecommunications division.

"We... expect strong (property) development profits between 1998-2002, with an estimated pre-tax profit of HK$12.3 billion coming from an attributable development landbank of about 4.7 million square feet," Merrill Lynch said.

It said gross rental income would rise 86 percent to HK$3.4 billion from HK$1.9 billion over 1996-2000 after completion of new investment properties which raise Hutchison's existing portfolio in Hong Kong by 30 percent.

Hutchison's telecommunications division was expected to turn losses of HK$458 million in 1996 into core profits of HK$2.3 billion by 2000 and the company was likely to undergo further corporate restructuring, Merrill Lynch said.

Possible restructuring moves included a spin-off of Hong Kong International Terminals, Hutchison Ports International Holdings, Hutchison Delta Ports, Hutchison Max, PRC port interests and retailing and manufacturing operations, it said.
Merrill Lynch said it expected Hutchison's earnings derived from China to rise over 10 times to account for six percent of net profits in 1999 and about 16 percent of net profits by 2004.
